paper_title: LensAge index as a deep learning-based biological age for self-monitoring the risks of age-related diseases and mortality
prediction_task: Biological age estimation from anterior segment photos → disease and mortality risk prediction

reviewer_concerns.concern_text: All datasets consisted of participants from China only. Single-ethnicity training from a single national screening program. LensAge DL model may be limited in generalizability to other populations.
reviewer_concerns.author_response: Acknowledged generalizability limitation and discussed plans for multi-ethnic validation.

reviewer_concerns.concern_text: What was defined as 'healthy individuals' for training? Were patients screened for diseases or self-reported absence sufficient? How to account for patients with undiagnosed diseases? Were corticosteroid users excluded (secondary cataracts)?
reviewer_concerns.author_response: Added detailed inclusion/exclusion criteria with disease screening protocol.

reviewer_concerns.concern_text: A variety of slit-lamps were used (BQ-900, BX-900, OVS-II, PSL-Classic). Did every participant have photographs from all slit-lamps? What was the distribution of slit-lamp models in the dataset?
reviewer_concerns.author_response: Added device distribution analysis and robustness to different slit-lamp models.

reviewer_concerns.concern_text: Explainability analysis needed — what specific lens features drive the LensAge prediction? Is it nuclear sclerosis, cortical changes, posterior subcapsular changes? Grad-CAM only shows where, not what.
reviewer_concerns.author_response: Added ophthalmologist-graded lens feature correlation analysis.

reviewer_strengths.text: Novel research question. Demonstrated that LensAge and LensAge index are accurate indicators of age-related disease risks. Non-invasive method for biological age assessment.
